scope: Nine remaining p1716 latent-structure, clustering, signal and eigenpair interfaces; direct source inspection and verified library comparisons.

Inspected Setoid/Basic:76–80, Multiset/Sort:26–59, Eigenspace/Basic:424–446, InnerProductSpace/Spectrum:429–454, Monotone/Defs:79–87 and Finset sum-div:26–27; reused inspected extrema, log/power, integral and filter declarations. rows.result: Setoid.ker of the true break-time map on the broken-subject subtype identifies equal break times; strict monotonicity can order the distinct values. These do not infer the unknown cluster count or an estimated partition.
rows.gap: Identify the source latent groups with the nonempty fibers of the true break-time map and supply their ordered finite indexing.

comparisons.D18: Restrict the domain to C-bullet, use tau_i as the fiber map, and index its distinct values by b_1<...<b_K0. The displayed common-value, disjointness and coverage conditions correspond to these fibers when the conventional nonempty partition interpretation is supplied. Keep this latent structure separate from estimated clusters and K-hat. Do not import the adjacent common-break wording as equality of all strictly ordered b_k; only K0=1 is compatible with that special case.

rows.result: StrictMono expresses the strict ordering of proportional break locations; finite set cardinalities give the cluster and total broken-subject sizes. Arithmetic then states the exact proportional identities.
rows.gap: Package the ordered interior break fractions and positive cluster proportions with the source’s exact integrality and asymptotic conventions.

comparisons.D22: Preserve b_k=c_k*T with 0<c_1<...<c_K0<1 and |C(b_k)|=d_k*|C-bullet|, d_k>0 and sum d_k=1. Set.encard is finite on subject subsets, but a real proportional-size equation requires justified conversion of those finite counts. These are exact equalities, not rounded approximate limits; admissible integer sample subsequences and uniformity of c_k,d_k are not fixed by generic arithmetic. Theorem 4 cites this part specifically, without thereby importing 2(ii).

rows.result: Finite min-prime represents the least jump norm only with a nonempty true broken set. The conditional-supremum comparison can represent uniform norm upper bounds on nonempty bounded value sets; neither declaration proves a statistical signal separation.
rows.gap: State the uniform mean/jump bounds and positive lower jump bound with an explicit nonempty support and the intended uniformity regime.

comparisons.D23: Assumption 2(ii) bounds both ||mu_i|| and ||delta_i|| uniformly over subjects and bounds min_{i in C-bullet}||delta_i|| away from zero. Supply a common upper constant and positive lower constant in the intended regime; separately finite maxima for each N do not automatically give the required uniform control. The source does not define a minimum for an empty true broken set. Norms use the source L2 interpretation, and this part is explicitly assumed in Theorem 3 rather than added to Theorem 4 by analogy.

rows.result: Tendsto can state convergence of the penalty to zero and divergence of its rescaled value to positive infinity; real logarithm and power give the printed deterministic scale on its valid large-index domain.
rows.gap: Express both penalty limits along the intended N,T regime while retaining the quantifier over every positive zeta.

comparisons.D24: Keep one rho_NT sequence satisfying rho_NT→0 and, for every zeta>0, T*rho_NT/[log(max(N,T))]^(1+zeta)→+infinity. Use the same sequence for all zeta, not an existentially chosen power or a zeta-dependent penalty. Do not add an unstated relation N(T) or treat totalized division/log values at small indices as finite-sample conventions. This is a tuning condition explicitly referenced by the criterion construction; it does not by itself prove consistent K selection.

rows.result: Multiset.sort produces a sorted list with every repeated estimated time retained, as confirmed by sort_eq; ordinary list indexing and arithmetic form adjacent gaps. It does not choose among equal ranked gaps or certify nonempty candidate clusters.
rows.gap: Assemble the largest-gap clustering rule while retaining unspecified gap ties, candidate feasibility and the final half-open endpoint.

comparisons.D19: Collect one tau-hat_i per detected subject as a multiset; sorting a Finset of distinct time values would incorrectly discard repetitions. Form all n-1 adjacent gaps, choose the K-1 largest with their right endpoints, sort those boundaries and assign original subject indices through [lower,upper) intervals. Equal gap values may have different right endpoints, so the source still needs a selection convention. Preserve boundaries 1 and T and the strict upper bound, which excludes estimated time T; no interval closure, K≤n constraint or repair of coincident/empty clusters is supplied by sorting.

rows.result: Finite normalized scalar sums express average break estimates and residual averages; indicator expresses the fitted step mean, log expresses the penalty criterion on positive residuals, and IsMinOn supplies minimality without membership or selection.
rows.gap: Define the fitted criterion on a valid clustering and segment domain, preserving the missing noninteger-break and logarithm conventions before selecting its minimizer.

comparisons.D21: Keep the average tau-hat_{k|K}, pre/post means, residual V(K), log(V(K))+K*rho_NT and final cluster relabeling in their printed order. Scalar sum-div applies to average time indices and residual values; vector mean functions still need their own scalar action. The average of integer break estimates may be noninteger yet appears directly as a summation endpoint: do not insert floor, rounding or interpolation. Empty clusters/detected sets, zero segment lengths and V(K)=0 are unspecified; Real.log 0=0 or field division by zero is not a source convention. Require K in [1,K-bar] separately from IsMinOn and preserve missing feasibility/tie rules; the reference to Assumption 2(iii) remains a construction dependency.

rows.result: Finite sums of subject squared integrals define each time-grid objective; IsMaxOn expresses maximality and max-prime supplies a finite largest objective value once the grid and values are well-defined. Neither selects the index or identifies estimated and true groups.
rows.gap: Construct the pooled CUSUM maximizer over estimated groups with explicit time-grid membership and retained exceptional-event conventions.

comparisons.D25: Equation (4.13) sums integrated squares of Z_iT over i in C-hat(b_k), then maximizes over integer t=1,...,T; it does not square an averaged CUSUM. Use measurable finite squared integrals or justified L2 norm squares, and require candidate membership alongside IsMaxOn. The returned object is a time index, not the maximum value. Preserve estimated group membership rather than replacing it with true groups; ties, empty estimated groups and indexing when K-hat differs from K0 remain unspecified. Exact recovery in Theorem 4 is a separate assertion.

rows.result: The finite maximum and convergence predicate represent the first signal condition; the nonnegative integral, floored partial sum and supremum represent the second after their domain/finiteness conditions are established.
rows.gap: Define both alternative regions with the source limit regimes and distinct mean-path centering, preserving their union rather than identifying them.

comparisons.D14: H_A-diamond adds divergence of max_i T*omega_Ti^2*||delta_i||^2/xi_NT, with omega_Ti=min(tau_i/T,1-tau_i/T). H-tilde_A-diamond permits that condition OR divergence of the deterministic mean-path supremum; it is not a conjunction. In (3.9) the centering is x, rather than floor(T*x)/T, and its normalization is 1/sqrt(T), with no added sqrt(N). Thus the step-constant grid reduction for the data CUSUM cannot simply be reused. Retain the threshold’s valid asymptotic domain and the corrected D8 mean-subscript ambiguity before asserting its decomposition.

rows.result: HasEigenvector gives the nonzero eigenpair relation in arbitrary module dimension; AntitoneOn supplies nonincreasing scalar order. The inspected compact self-adjoint spectral theorem gives trivial orthogonal complement of all eigenspaces on a complete Hilbert space, but requires compactness and symmetry and supplies no trace bound or particular enumeration.
rows.gap: Construct the source integral operator’s ordered nonnegative eigenpairs with the required spectral existence, normalization and summability justification.

comparisons.D6: Apply HasEigenvector to the underlying real linear endomorphism of Omega-tilde, with nonzero psi_k, eigenvalue lambda_k≥0 and a nonincreasing index sequence. Do not use the finite-dimensional eigenvalues array for the paper’s infinite sequence. The source’s positivity and pointwise kernel-limit wording alone do not establish the compactness, self-adjointness and complete-space premises of the inspected spectral theorem, nor a countable orthonormal basis, trace summability or convergence of the Brownian-bridge series. L2 quotient equality also differs from an unqualified pointwise equation in representatives; retain the source convention gap.
